package_info.package_name: Fake Microsoft Visual Studio Installer (Cookie Stealer)
package_info.package_manager: N/A (Distributed as a deceptive installer via phishing/third-party sites)
package_info.why_malicious: The installer impersonates the official Microsoft Visual Studio installer but instead deploys a Cookie Stealer malware. It is distributed through phishing campaigns, social engineering, and malicious advertisements, with the intent to extract browser cookies and other sensitive data from the victim's system and exfiltrate them to an attacker-controlled server.

execution_context.trigger: Upon execution of the fake installer binary
execution_context.file_location: Malicious Visual Studio installer executable (e.g., Setup.exe or similarly named file in the download directory)
required_permissions: filesystem (read access to browser profile directories)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: The code enumerates browser profile directories for Chrome, Edge, and Firefox, locates and reads cookie storage files (such as 'Cookies' for Chromium-based browsers and 'cookies.sqlite' for Firefox), decrypts stored cookies using system APIs or hardcoded decryption routines, and transmits the extracted cookie data to a hardcoded remote command-and-control (C2) server via HTTP POST requests.
malicious_snippets.code_language: Compiled executable (likely C++ or C#, or Python bundled as EXE via PyInstaller or similar tool)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Upon execution of the installer, the code scans browser profile directories, reads and decrypts browser cookie files, then sends the extracted cookie data via HTTP POST to a hardcoded remote server, resulting in theft of session credentials and user data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Accessing and exfiltrating browser cookies is not a legitimate action for any installer, especially one claiming to be from Microsoft. The code's behavior of decrypting and transmitting sensitive user data to an external server is a clear indicator of credential theft.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A genuine Visual Studio installer should only install development tools and dependencies, never access browser data or perform network exfiltration of user credentials.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise security or compliance tools may access browser data for auditing, but only with explicit user consent and never transmit it to untrusted or unknown servers.
key_indicators: Direct access to browser profile directories (e.g., AppData\Local\Google\Chrome\User Data, AppData\Roaming\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles)
Reading and decrypting browser cookie storage files ('Cookies', 'cookies.sqlite')
Outbound HTTP POST requests to hardcoded, non-Microsoft domains immediately after installer execution
Installer binary is unsigned or signed with an untrusted certificate
Masquerading as a legitimate Microsoft Visual Studio installer

attack_chain.action: Victim is lured to download and execute a fake Visual Studio installer via phishing emails, social engineering, or malicious advertisements.
Upon execution, the malicious installer scans the system for browser profile directories and extracts stored cookies.
attack_chain.leads_to: Collection of sensitive browser cookie data

attack_chain.action: The installer decrypts the extracted cookies and sends them to a remote attacker-controlled C2 server via HTTP POST.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to victim's web sessions and online accounts

behavioral_signatures: Installer processes (e.g., Setup.exe) accessing browser profile directories immediately after launch
Unexpected read operations on browser cookie files ('Cookies', 'cookies.sqlite') by installer binaries
Outbound HTTP POST requests from installer processes to non-Microsoft or suspicious domains
Execution of unsigned or suspiciously signed installer binaries masquerading as Microsoft products
file_indicators: Installer executables named similarly to official Visual Studio installers but not signed by Microsoft
Presence of installer files downloaded from non-official Microsoft sources
Temporary files or artifacts created in browser profile directories during installer execution
Unusual access timestamps on browser cookie files coinciding with installer execution
network_indicators: HTTP POST requests to hardcoded or suspicious domains/IPs not associated with Microsoft immediately after installer execution
Connections to known C2 infrastructure or domains previously linked to cookie stealer malware
Outbound traffic from installer binaries to IP addresses or domains flagged in threat intelligence feeds
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for installer processes accessing browser cookie storage locations and initiating outbound HTTP POST requests to untrusted or non-Microsoft domains. Flag unsigned or suspiciously signed Visual Studio installers, especially those downloaded from unofficial sources. Correlate process execution with file access and network activity to identify cookie exfiltration attempts. Alert on anomalous access to browser cookie files by non-browser processes, particularly during or immediately after installer execution.
